description: GOLDEN: a well-formed exploratory report. Every artifact is registered once and referenced by id, every finding carries the four fields a reader cannot reconstruct (actual, expected, repro, fixDirection), the run states its own boundaries in scope.notCovered, the executive verdict agrees with the severity counts, and a score is reported only for a dimension that was actually run. This is the shape the skill's procedure produces; if it stops passing, the pipeline regressed.

input.scenario: An authenticated pass over a checkout flow, with one high finding that was reproduced and investigated.

output.title: Example Shop checkout
output.summary: Checkout completes end to end, but the order total shown at the confirmation step disagrees with the total the API charged whenever a percentage discount is applied.

scope.objective: Establish whether a customer can complete a purchase with a discount code applied, and whether the amount shown matches the amount charged.
covered: Adding two items to the basket and applying the discount code SAVE10 at /checkout
The confirmation step, including the order summary panel and the Pay button
The POST /api/orders request and the totals it returns
notCovered: Card payment was never completed — the run must not create a real charge, and the sandbox gateway was not available on staging.
Accessibility was not examined in this run; it needs a dedicated pass before release.
Real-world latency cannot be measured here — staging sits on the same network as the test runner.

executive.headline: Customers applying a discount are shown a total the system does not charge them.
executive.health: The checkout flow itself is sound: the basket, the discount field, and the order request all behave correctly. The defect is a rounding disagreement between the total the page renders and the total the API returns.
risks: A customer sees £44.99 and is charged £45.00 whenever a percentage discount rounds to a half penny.
The mismatch is silent — nothing in the UI reconciles the two figures.
executive.recommendedAction: Fix the rounding so the displayed total is taken from the API response rather than recomputed client-side, then re-run this pass.

performance.note: Measured on staging over a local network; production sits behind a CDN and will differ.

evidence.description: The order summary panel showing the discounted total
The order request and the totals the API returned

findings.title: Displayed order total disagrees with the amount the API charges
findings.actual: With SAVE10 applied to a £49.99 basket, the order summary renders £44.99 while POST /api/orders returns and charges 4500 pence (£45.00). The page never reconciles the two, so the customer is shown one figure and billed another.
findings.expected: The total on screen is the total that will be charged. Where they can differ, the page shows the API's figure rather than a locally recomputed one.
findings.repro:
1. Sign in as a customer
2. Add two items totalling £49.99 to the basket
3. Open /checkout and apply the code SAVE10
4. Compare the summary total with the amount in the POST /api/orders response
steps: Add two items totalling £49.99 to the basket
Open /checkout and apply the discount code SAVE10
Read the total in the order summary panel
Compare it with the `total` field in the POST /api/orders response
findings.businessImpact: Every discounted order shows a price the customer is not charged. Individually it is a penny; collectively it is a consumer-pricing accuracy issue, and it is the kind of discrepancy that generates support contacts and chargebacks rather than being absorbed quietly.
findings.fixDirection: Render the total from the API response instead of recomputing it in the basket component, or move the rounding to a single shared helper used by both sides.

rootCause.summary: The client rounds the discount down while the server rounds the final total to the nearest penny, so the two disagree by one penny on any half-penny result.
chain: The basket component computes discount = subtotal * 0.10 and truncates to two decimals.
The API computes the discount in integer pence and rounds the final total half-up.
A £49.99 subtotal produces a 4.999 discount, truncated to 4.99 on the client and rounded to 5.00 on the server.
Nothing compares the rendered total with the response, so the difference never surfaces.

regressionRisk.note: Totals are rendered in the basket, the checkout summary, and the confirmation email.
retest: A discounted order shows the same total on the summary and the confirmation
A discount that lands exactly on a penny still rounds correctly

cases.title: Displayed total matches the charged total
An invalid discount code is rejected

whatWorksWell: The basket updates correctly when items are added and removed.
An invalid discount code is rejected with a message naming the field.
fixOrder: EXP-1 — reconcile the displayed total with the charged total

recommendations.action: Render monetary totals from the API response rather than recomputing them client-side
recommendations.rationale: Removes the whole class of client/server rounding disagreement, not just this instance.
